Position Overview:

The Solution Architect is responsible for owning and shaping technical solutions at the value-stream and product level, ensuring architectural alignment, scalability, and adherence to Guardian standards. This role is hands-on and execution-oriented, partnering closely with Tech Leads, Product Owners, and delivery teams to translate business needs into sound, secure, and resilient technology solutions.

This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains.

The Solution Architect focuses on solution design, delivery enablement, and technical problem solving, building solutions while collaborating with Business stakeholders, Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to align with broader enterprise patterns.

Key Responsibilities:

• Owns product/team-level solution design and delivery architecture
• Works with Principal Solution Architect for patterns/guardrails; Head of Portfolio Architecture for BU priorities; Principal Enterprise Architect only when enterprise exceptions or cross-domain conflicts arise
• Own product- and team-level technical architecture decisions within a value stream.
• Design and document solution architectures, including application, integration, data, and infrastructure components.
• Partner with Product Owners and Tech Leads to align roadmaps, MVP scope, and technical trade-offs.
• Ensure solutions follow Guardian architecture standards, security requirements, and design patterns.
• Collaborate with Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to reuse enterprise capabilities where appropriate.
• Identify, manage, and help resolve technical dependencies and impediments impacting delivery.
• Provide hands-on guidance to teams on design quality, code structure, and technical approaches.
• Lead proof-of-concepts for new business capabilities, Influencing Technology Strategy, Solution Design, Architecture Standards.
• Mentor engineers on architecture principles, design decisions, and problem-solving techniques.
• Continuously look for opportunities to simplify designs, reduce technical debt, and improve delivery efficiency.
• Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements.
• Available for production incidents with major impact to business operations

You Have:

• Strong experience designing and delivering enterprise-scale technology solutions.
• Working knowledge of cloud platforms, APIs, data integration, and modern application architectures.
• Experience collaborating within Agile / product-based delivery models.
• Experience in designing hybrid architectures where applications reside both on-premise and public cloud including understanding of cloud provider services.
• Proven track record of architecting solutions that demand operating large scale business critical systems in Insurance domain.

At Kyndryl, we design, build, manage and modernize the mission-critical technology systems that the world depends on every day. So why work at Kyndryl? The Role

Job Description

Your role

As a Design Ops Associate, you’ll help create the structure, tools, and processes that enable design teams to do their best work. Rather than creating design deliverables yourself, you’ll focus on improving how design work is planned, coordinated, tracked, and delivered across projects and teams. This role balances operational planning with day-to-day execution, helping designers spend more time solving customer problems and less time navigating process challenges.

You’ll work closely with designers, product teams, engineers, and delivery partners to support the successful execution of design initiatives. Your work will help create visibility into priorities, timelines, dependencies, and outcomes, enabling teams to collaborate more effectively and make informed decisions.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone interested in design operations, programme coordination, process improvement, and the ways design teams operate within large organisations. You’ll gain exposure to design systems, digital product development, experience design practices, and portfolio management while building valuable operational and consulting skills that can support multiple career paths.

What you will do

Enable effective design delivery

• Support planning activities for design projects, including intake, prioritisation, scheduling, and resource coordination

Coordinate across teams

Improve operational effectiveness

Support portfolio oversight

• Maintain information that helps teams understand workload, capacity, and priorities
• Assist with forecasting, planning, and operational reporting activities
• Monitor progress against agreed objectives and highlight potential risks or constraints

Learn and grow

• Build knowledge of DesignOps, experience design, and digital product development practices
• Learn how design teams collaborate within large-scale customer environments
• Develop skills in programme coordination, process improvement, stakeholder management, and operational planning
• Gain hands-on experience using planning, collaboration, and workflow management tools

jobs.description: Job Description The Team: The Display Design and Development group is a dynamic, cross-functional hardware organization within GM’s Compute & Connectivity Hardware team, responsible for the end-to-end design and integration of next-generation in-vehicle display modules. The team owns the electrical and mechanical design of fully integrated display systems—spanning control boards, optics, mechanics, and firmware—while also reviewing and approving supplier and production design changes to ensure robustness, quality, and cost efficiency. Working closely with software, vehicle integration, and design partners, the group is building an in-house display platform that can be reused across programs, enabling faster technology introduction, richer digital experiences, and a more consistent, premium display experience for customers. The Role: We are looking for a Staff Hardware Engineer to lead hardware definition and technical execution for display-focused diagnostic and interface integration work. This role is centered on display hardware bring-up, interface definition, issue investigation, and cross-functional problem solving, with particular emphasis on diagnostic architecture, FIDM and related interface documentation, and PRTS issue resolution. The ideal candidate combines strong display hardware fundamentals with the ability to work across system, software, validation, and supplier teams to define robust hardware requirements, drive root-cause investigations, and improve product quality and launch readiness. What You'll Do (Responsibilities): Lead hardware definition and technical execution for display-related diagnostic and interface work. Own and refine FIDM and other interface documentation needed to support system integration and issue resolution. Drive Display Diagnostic 2.0 related hardware definition, implementation alignment, and technical problem solving. Investigate hardware and system issues identified through PRTS and lead cross-functional root-cause analysis. Support display ECU and subsystem bring-up, debugging, and validation. Translate system-level needs into clear hardware requirements, interface definitions, and engineering actions. Work closely with software, systems, validation, packaging, and supplier teams to resolve integration issues efficiently. Review schematics, interface definitions, and hardware design decisions for technical completeness and robustness. Identify design, integration, and validation gaps early and drive corrective actions. Support sourcing, development, and launch activities by providing technical leadership in the display hardware domain. Help improve engineering processes for issue tracking, documentation quality, and diagnostic readiness. What Success Looks Like: Diagnostic and interface requirements are clear, complete, and actionable. FIDM and related documents are maintained at a level that improves integration efficiency. PRTS issues are resolved with strong technical ownership and disciplined root-cause analysis. Hardware and system issues are identified earlier and closed faster. Cross-functional teams view this role as a key technical anchor for display hardware diagnostics and integration. Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications): Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field. Significant experience in automotive hardware engineering, with direct experience in display or ECU-related development. Experience with diagnostic architecture, failure analysis, and serviceability considerations. Familiarity with PRTS-driven issue management and structured engineering problem solving. Perplexity is seeking an experienced Machine Learning Engineer to improve search quality across the middle and later stages of ranking. We are looking for a strong ranking generalist who can own ambiguous problems end to end and brings exceptional depth in either neural ranking or production ranking systems.

Responsibilities

- Relentlessly push search quality forward through models, data, evaluation, infrastructure, or any other leverage available.

- Own ranking-quality problems end to end: define the evaluation, identify the bottleneck, build the solution, and ship it safely.

- Train and evaluate retrieval, ranking, and classification models, including neural and LLM-based approaches where appropriate.

- Build and operate ranking infrastructure, including feature computation, low-latency inference, multi-stage cascades, deployment, and monitoring.

- Make sound trade-offs across quality, latency, reliability, cost, and engineering complexity.

- Collaborate across Data, AI, Infrastructure, and Product while retaining ownership of the final quality outcome.

Qualifications

- Deep understanding of search or recommender systems and their evaluation.

- Proven ownership of a large-scale production ranking system or a substantial class of quality problems.

- Strong machine-learning and software-engineering skills across data, models, serving, and monitoring.

- Ability to drive ambiguous, cross-team problems without continuous task decomposition.

- Exceptional depth in either modern neural ranking methods or low-latency ranking systems and runtime.

- Minimum 5 years of relevant industry experience.
